intro: To add a text box in Numbers on Mac, open your spreadsheet and click the Text button in the toolbar. A box appears on the sheet, so drag it where you want it and type over the placeholder text.
tldr: Open the spreadsheet, then click the Text button in the Numbers toolbar. A box appears on the sheet.
Drag the box where you want it, then click inside and type over the placeholder text.
If the box will not move, click outside it, then click the text once to select the box.
Resize with the handle on the left or right side. Set a default style from Format > Advanced > Set as Default Text Box Appearance.

blocks.text: A text box in Numbers is a block of text that sits on the sheet, not inside a cell. That makes it the right tool for a title, a footnote, or a note beside a chart. Use a cell when the words belong in a table row. Use a text box when the words should stay in one place while the table changes. The steps are short, and most of the work happens in the toolbar.
Add the text box from the toolbar

Apple's guide for Numbers on Mac gives one route. Open the spreadsheet and click the Text button in the toolbar. A box appears on the sheet. The guide does not describe an Insert menu option, and it does not list a keyboard shortcut. The toolbar is the place to start, so the numbered steps below follow that route.
Type into the box and move it into place

A new box shows placeholder text. Click inside it and type. Your words replace the placeholder, so you do not need to delete it first. To move the box, drag it to the spot you want on the sheet. Let go when the box sits where it belongs. Positioning takes one drag, so you do not need to be exact on the first try.
When the text box will not move

Sometimes the box refuses to move. That usually happens because the words inside the box are selected, not the box itself. Click outside the box to clear the selection. Then click the text once. That selects the box, and you can drag it again. Apple's guide describes this fix for the Mac app.
Resize the box and control the font size

Resize the box with the selection handle on its left or right side. Drag the handle in to narrow the box, or out to widen it. By default Numbers changes the font size so the text fits inside the box. That helps with short labels. With a long note, the text can shrink further than you expect, so check it at normal zoom.

If you want a fixed font size, Apple's guide gives a different route. Select the box, then choose Format > Shapes and Lines > Reset Text and Object handles. I could not test that menu on a live copy of Numbers while writing this page. The path comes from Apple's text, so confirm the menu names on your version before you rely on them.
Delete a text box cleanly

Click the box until a blue outline appears around it. Then press Delete. The outline is your check. If you only see a cursor in the words, you have selected the text, not the box. Look at the outline before you press Delete. That way you do not clear a cell or other content by mistake.
Set a default style for new text boxes

Say you want every note on the sheet in the same font, color, and alignment. Build one box that looks right. Select it. Then go to Format > Advanced > Set as Default Text Box Appearance. New boxes should start from that look, so you do not repeat the setup each time. Test one new box before you trust the default.
A worked example: titling a budget sheet

Say you have a sheet with a monthly budget table in the middle. You want a title above the table, a source note below it, and a short key in the corner. Start with the title. Click the Text button, drag the box above the table, and type. Then resize it so the box spans the table width.

Next, add the source note with the same steps. Drag it below the table. Let the font auto fit if the note is short. Use the fixed font route if you want the note to match the title size. Last, add the key. If every label should look alike, set the first box as the default before you add the rest.

blocks.text: Common mistakes people make with text boxes

items: Typing before the box is selected. Click the box first, so your words land in it.
Keeping numbers in a text box. Text boxes sit outside the grid. Put figures you want to calculate in cells.
Trusting auto fit on a long note. The text can shrink until it is hard to read.
Assuming every version has the same menus. Check Numbers > About Numbers before you follow a menu path.
Building the same style by hand each time. Set a default once instead.

blocks.text: When a text box is the wrong tool

A text box works for words, not for values you want to total. If a label belongs to a column, put it in the table's header row. That keeps it attached to the data when you sort or filter. The [sort a table guide](/how-to/sort-a-table-by-column-in-numbers) explains how the table side works.
Headers and footers need a different approach

Header and footer boxes cause more trouble than regular text boxes. A community thread about Numbers 13.x suggests File > Print, then clicking one of the three boxes in the header or footer and typing. Apple has not confirmed that route in its guides. Some users in the thread said it did not work. Test it on a copy of the file first.
Numbers for iCloud and newer macOS releases

Numbers for iCloud runs in a browser at icloud.com/numbers. Apple's iCloud guide gives the same core steps. Click the Text button, drag the box into position, and type. To delete, select the box and press Delete. The iCloud guide gives no menu paths or keyboard shortcuts, so the Mac guide is the better source for menus.

Apple's newer features sit behind a subscription. Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 a month or $129 a year in the U.S. Apple says a free version of Numbers remains available. The new Numbers AI assistant needs macOS 27 or later, is in beta, and works in U.S. English only.
Check your Numbers version before you follow menus

Apple's Mac guide is labeled Numbers 15.4. Wikipedia lists 15.4 as the stable release, dated September 29, 2026. Apple has not confirmed that date in the pages reviewed for this guide. Apple released Numbers for macOS 15.1 as a new app on January 28, 2026. It removed older Mac builds from the App Store on April 13, 2026. Open Numbers, choose Numbers > About Numbers, and compare the version with the guide.
Where to go next with your spreadsheet

Once the box is in place, you may want a table under it. The [table guide](/how-to/add-a-table-in-numbers) covers the Table button, styles, and resizing. For faster editing, [keyboard shortcuts in Numbers](/how-to/use-keyboard-shortcuts-in-numbers) lists the keys worth learning. If the file goes to someone else, [share a spreadsheet in Numbers](/how-to/share-a-spreadsheet-in-numbers) walks through invites and links.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to add a text box in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's Mac guide for Numbers does not list one. I could not find a shortcut for this action in Apple's documentation. Treat that as none documented, not as proof that none exists. The Text button in the toolbar is the route Apple describes.

faq.question: Where is the Text button in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's guide names it only as the Text button in the toolbar, which runs along the top of the window. Hover over the toolbar icons and read the tooltip. Labels can differ slightly between versions, so the tooltip is your best check.

faq.question: Can I add a text box in Numbers for iCloud?
faq.answer: Yes. Go to icloud.com/numbers, open a spreadsheet, click the Text button, drag the box into position, and type. Apple's iCloud guide gives no menu paths or keyboard shortcuts for this task.

faq.question: Why did my text shrink when I resized the box?
faq.answer: By default Numbers changes the font size so the text fits inside the box. Widen the box to give the text more room. For a fixed font size, select the box and use Format > Shapes and Lines > Reset Text and Object handles.

faq.question: Do I need a subscription to add text boxes in Numbers?
faq.answer: The text box steps in Apple's guide do not mention a subscription. Apple says a free version of Numbers remains available. The newer Numbers intelligence features belong to Apple Creator Studio, which costs $12.99 a month or $129 a year in the U.S.

faq.question: Can I put a text box in a header or footer?
faq.answer: Header and footer boxes need a different route. A community thread about Numbers 13.x suggests File > Print, then clicking one of the boxes in the header or footer. Apple has not confirmed that route, so test it on a copy first.

steps.name: Open the spreadsheet
steps.text: Open the spreadsheet in Numbers on your Mac. Go to the sheet where the text belongs. The new box lands on the sheet you have open, so check the sheet first.
steps.tip: If the box belongs on a different sheet, switch sheets before you click the Text button.

steps.name: Click the Text button
steps.text: Find the Text button in the toolbar at the top of the window. Click it once. A text box appears on the sheet with placeholder text inside.
steps.tip: Apple's guide names the control only as the Text button. Read the tooltip on your version to confirm the label.

steps.name: Drag the box into place
steps.text: Drag the box to the spot you want on the sheet. Let go when the box sits where you need it.

steps.name: Type over the placeholder
steps.text: Click inside the box and type. Your words replace the placeholder text, so you do not need to delete it first.
steps.tip: If you cannot type, the text may not be selected. Click outside the box, then click the text once.

steps.name: Resize the box
steps.text: Drag the selection handle on the left or right side of the box. Drag in to narrow it, and out to widen it. By default the font size changes to fit inside the box.
steps.tip: Short labels look best with auto fit. A long note may shrink more than you want, so check it at normal zoom.

steps.name: Delete a box you no longer need
steps.text: Click the box until a blue outline appears around it. Then press Delete.
steps.tip: Check for the blue outline first, so you do not clear a cell by mistake.

troubleshooting.problem: The text box will not move or select
troubleshooting.fix: Click outside the box to deselect the text. Then click the text once to select the box itself. Drag it again. This is the fix in Apple's Mac guide.

troubleshooting.problem: Typing does not work in a header or footer
troubleshooting.fix: Try File > Print, then click one of the three boxes in the header or footer and type. This comes from a Numbers 13.x community thread, not from Apple. Some users said it did not work, so check the result.

troubleshooting.problem: Cells will not select in the sheet
troubleshooting.fix: The sheet may still be in Print view. Click Done in the lower-right corner. A community thread about a Numbers spreadsheet describes this fix.

troubleshooting.problem: Text shrinks too small after resizing
troubleshooting.fix: Widen the box, or select it and use Format > Shapes and Lines > Reset Text and Object handles for a fixed font size. The menu path comes from Apple's text and was not tested on a live copy of the app.
